items: It only pushes on **1 stroke out of 4**
The rest of the time the crank **coasts** on the flywheel
Give each one a **different turn** to fire
The bangs **overlap**, so the push never really stops

blocks.caption: Switch between 1, 2 and 4 cylinders. Watch the push graph fill in.
blocks.narration: Start with one cylinder and watch the push graph. Then switch to four and see how the gaps disappear.

lines: = 2 power strokes every turn, one every 180°
blocks.say: One cylinder gives one power stroke every two turns. Four cylinders give four every two turns, which is two every turn, or one every hundred and eighty degrees.

blocks.title: Hear it
blocks.text: A V8 sounds like a smooth rumble; a single-cylinder dirt bike sounds like a machine gun. More cylinders = more, smaller bangs, closer together.

items: Fuel + air burn → hot gas → pressure pushes the piston
The crankshaft turns the push into spin
Four strokes: intake, compression, power, exhaust. Two crank turns.
The camshaft opens the valves at half crank speed
Higher compression = more efficient, until it knocks
More cylinders firing in turns = smoother power

blocks.question: A common firing order for an inline-four is…
blocks.explain: 1-3-4-2 alternates between the ends of the engine to keep the crankshaft balanced.

blocks.question: In a 4-cylinder engine, how many power strokes happen per crankshaft turn?
blocks.explain: 4 power strokes over 2 turns = 2 per turn, one every 180°.
